reason: The cited evidence supports that plasma nitriding can harden Ti alloys and that low-temperature processing avoids degradation (E1), and that Ti-N layers improve hardness, wear, and corrosion resistance (E2). However, the specific claims about oxygen disrupting TiN, forming a porous stress-buffering sublayer, and the two-stage oxy-nitriding process are not supported by the cited passages.
premises: Low-temperature plasma nitriding can avoid mechanical degradation and phase transformation seen in high-temperature nitriding of Ti alloys
Oxygen addition during nitriding can disrupt continuous TiN layer formation
A porous sublayer can act as a stress buffer to reduce crack initiation
Discontinuous TiN phases (ε-Ti2N/δ-TiN) can form a hardened compound layer
Plasma oxy-nitriding at ~650 °C can improve hardness and wear resistance without sacrificing ductility and corrosion resistance
